newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti Infostrada talks progressing well.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti Infostrada talks progressing well.

text.p: Olivetti Chief Executive Roberto Colaninno said that talks with France Telecom about the French company joining its Infostrada fixed-line telecoms joint venture were progressing well.

"We are at a good point in the talks," Colaninno told daily newspaper Corriere Della Sera when asked about France Telecom's move to join the Infostrada venture, which is 67 percent owned by Olivetti and 33 percent by U.S. group Bell Atlantic.

Olivetti and France Telecom had been talking at least since November 1995 when Infostrada announced a joint venture with the French group to set up Italy's second major fixed-line telecoms network. The two groups moved closer in August 1996 when they reached an agreement together to buy a 70 percent stake in the Italian state railway's domestic phone network.

Analysts have said it was logical for France Telecom to join Infostrada, but have doubted whether it would want to take a direct equity stake in Olivetti with the privatisation of France Telecom looming this year.
